newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bonds off with Treasuries, ValuJet gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bonds off with Treasuries, ValuJet gains.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds fell along with U.S. Treasuries in extremely light trade after surprisingly strong data bombarded the markets, dealers said.
Junk bonds overall were weak, off 1/4, but ValuJet Inc debt bucked the trend and gained more than a point after news the airline expects to return to the skies within the next month.
ValuJet was grounded following a May 11 crash in the Florida Everglades that killed 110 people.
ValuJet's $150 million senior unsecured debt gained to a 88-1/2 bid, 89-1/2 offer from Thursday's 87-1/4 bid.
Credit rating agency Standard & Poor's said it may still cut the notes' CCC-plus rating, along with its B-minus corporate credit rating.

"However, the U.S. Department of Transportation's preliminary approval yesterday for ValuJet Airlines to resume flight operations increases the likelihood that ratings will be affirmed at current levels and removed from CreditWatch," S&P said.
U.S. Treasuries stumbled over a point on the long-end after the Chicago Purchasing Managers index jumped to a surprising 60.0 in August versus 51.2 in July, analysts said.
At 1100 EDT/1600 GMT, the 30-year long bond was off 31/32 at 95-13/32 to yield 7.12 percent.
The equity markets also took a spill, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average off 46.61 at 5601.41.
The primary market was dead quiet with no deals firmly scheduled for Friday, syndicate officials said.
Next week's calender has yet to firm but light deal flow is expected in the run up to next Friday's U.S. employment report, they added.
The Public Securities Association has recommended a 1400 EDT/1800 GMT early close for the U.S. fixed-income markets on Friday in observance of the Labor Day holiday on Monday.
